teaser.text: CMOC Group Limited makes money by mining and processing metals and phosphate, then by trading metals through its wholly owned merchant, IXM. To understand how a dollar comes in and goes out, follow the material from rock to customer, and the cash from extraction through operating costs, governments, lenders and reinvestment.

stock.title: CMOC stock forecast
stock.meta_description: CMOC's weighted case reaches HKD20.63 by October 2029, with bear and bull outcomes of HKD7.15 and HKD37.85.
stock.opening: CMOC's weighted price reaches HKD20.63 in October 2029, with outcomes from HKD7.15 to HKD37.85. It hinges on whether production growth becomes durable cash despite copper prices, cobalt exports and project execution.
stock.closing: The full CMOC memo also answers how CMOC's business works, who its rivals are, how its management allocates capital, and what risks could change the case.

blocks.heading: Where could CMOC's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast's central case is a positive return with substantial downside risk. The weighted price is HKD15.86 in October 2027, a 15% total return including dividends. It rises to HKD17.98 in October 2028, a 33% return. By October 2029, it reaches HKD20.63, a 55% return.
At the final date, the bear case gives HKD7.15 and the bull case gives HKD37.85. That is a range from a 46% loss to a 182% gain, dividends included, against today's HKD14.19.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for CMOC?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA is the main operating assumption. The latest half-year run-rate proxy is RMB58,759 million, based on operating income and depreciation. The base case rounds this to RMB59,000 million for the first forecast date, then RMB63,000 million and RMB67,000 million, supported by production guidance and KFM Phase II. The bear case falls to RMB47,200 million, then RMB42,000 million and RMB39,100 million as copper spreads and cobalt cash conversion weaken. The bull case rises to RMB64,000 million, then RMB75,000 million and RMB86,000 million if copper markets, KFM execution and cobalt exports all cooperate. The base remains credible because reported EBITDA rose from RMB14,820 million in 2021 to RMB45,090 million in 2025, but that record includes a production ramp and favorable prices.

blocks.heading: How much cash does CMOC really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow also depends on definition. CMOC’s own measure was RMB13,260 million. A stricter measure deducts interest and lease payments as well as capital spending, showing what remains after those obligations.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for CMOC today?

paragraphs.text: A forward P/E is the share price divided by forecast earnings. On 15 October 2026, the H share traded at HK$14.19, equal to a forward P/E of 7.8x. That looks modest, but mining profits rise and fall with metal prices. Copper averaged US$13,083.97 per tonne in the first half of 2026, 38.73% above the prior year. Normalized earnings therefore mean profits estimated at ordinary prices, costs and production, not at an unusually favourable point in the cycle. A low P/E can be like buying a bakery on a profit forecast built around an unusually high cake price.

dividend.meta_description: CMOC dividend history, cash coverage, payout policy, forecast changes and dividend yield against the share price.
dividend.opening: CMOC’s dividend rose to RMB0.29 per share in 2025, and its cash covered the payout, with dividends absorbing 50.8% of free cash flow. CMOC’s dividend policy promises cash dividends above 40% of attributable profit for 2024–2026, subject to business needs.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines CMOC’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does CMOC pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise gradually in the base case from RMB0.38 to RMB0.42 and RMB0.46 per share. This extends the uninterrupted DPS growth from RMB0.07 in 2021 to RMB0.29 in 2025, but remains below the stated payout ambition because the 2025 distribution was only 30.08% of profit. The bear case gives RMB0.15 and then RMB0.12 as project spending and weaker cash conversion dominate. The bull case gives RMB0.55, RMB0.62 and RMB0.70, supported by the RMB1.54941 analyst EPS estimate and stronger cash realization.

blocks.heading: Does CMOC’s dividend come from its free cash flow?

paragraphs.text: CMOC’s cash first supported expansion and payouts, then helped rebuild financial strength. Free cash flow means operating cash left after capital spending. It was weak or negative from 2021 to 2023, while dividends still went out. In 2024, free cash flow improved sharply, but in 2025 dividends absorbed 50.8%. Working capital also matters: cash can be tied up in inventory or unpaid customer bills even when a mine reports accounting profit.
**Paid out, % of free cash flow** — Odin’s RMB2,842.67376053 million purchase raised the payout ratio; excluding it, shareholder payments were 40.2% of free cash flow.

paragraphs.text: CMOC’s dividend policy now promises cash dividends above 40% of attributable profit for 2024–2026, subject to business needs. Its first interim dividend, declared in 2026, changed payment timing but did not by itself prove the annual promise had been met. The real test is whether shareholder returns remain compatible with maintenance, new projects and financial resilience.

earnings.title: CMOC earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: CMOC's next results are expected on October 23, 2026; watch whether production becomes cash.
earnings.opening: CMOC's next results are expected on October 23, 2026. The key watch is whether operating cash keeps pace with production.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains CMOC's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: CMOC has promised more production in 2026, but production is only the first step toward cash.

The copper target requires the second half to do either slightly less than, or more than, the first half’s work, depending on where the annual range lands. Capacity describes a plant’s eventual operating speed, not what it will produce immediately. The guidance table sets out the ranges for metals, fertilizer and physical trade volume across periods.

blocks.heading: Did CMOC keep its past production promises?

paragraphs.text: The previous copper result shows why guidance needs testing against delivery. In 2025 CMOC produced 741,149 tonnes, or 118% of its guidance midpoint. That indicates strong execution, but it may also indicate conservative guidance. The next question is whether that operational strength becomes earnings.

blocks.heading: What is CMOC's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Quarterly revenue reached RMB68,916.69047487 million, approximately 41.3% above June 2025. Net income increased 77.6%. Gross margin rose from 20.0% to 23.1%, though it remained below December 2025’s 28.6%.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in CMOC's next results?

paragraphs.text: The first checkpoint is 23 October 2026, when CMOC’s board is scheduled to consider nine-month results. The reader should compare production with guidance, then ask whether operating cash keeps pace. A rising stockpile can make output look strong while absorbing money needed by contractors or lenders.
